Full Stack Web Development.title: API Gateway Peak Load Window
Full Stack Web Development.scenario: An enterprise API gateway logs the payload size (in kilobytes) of consecutive incoming HTTP requests. During traffic surges, backend engineers need to determine the maximum aggregate bandwidth processed across any continuous window of exactly K requests to configure rate-limiting buckets.
Full Stack Web Development.inputFormat:
Line 1: Two space-separated integers N and K, where N is the total number of requests and K is the sliding window size.
Line 2: N space-separated integers representing request payload sizes in kilobytes.
Full Stack Web Development.outputFormat: A single integer denoting the maximum sum of payload sizes across any contiguous block of K requests.

Data Science.title: Telemetry Sensor Stability Index
Data Science.scenario: A data science team is evaluating autonomous drone sensor streams. A telemetry stream is labeled VOLATILE if the difference between its maximum and minimum readings within a mission segment strictly exceeds a stability threshold T. Otherwise, it is labeled STABLE. Given N readings and threshold T, classify the stream and output the observed range (max - min).
Data Science.inputFormat:
Line 1: Two space-separated integers N and T, where N is the reading count and T is the stability threshold.
Line 2: N space-separated integers representing recorded sensor values.
Data Science.outputFormat: A single line containing the classification (VOLATILE or STABLE) followed by a space and the range (max - min).
Data Science.explanation: Maximum reading is 40 and minimum reading is 10. Range = 40 - 10 = 30. Since 30 > 25 (threshold T), the stream is VOLATILE 30.

Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learni.title: Model Confidence Discretizer
Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learni.scenario: An image classification neural network emits integer confidence scores (0 to 100) for a batch of predictions. The inference pipeline categorizes each prediction into: High (>= 80), Medium (50 to 79 inclusive), or Low (< 50). Compute the frequency of each category and the overall average confidence formatted to 1 decimal place.
Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learni.inputFormat:
Line 1: An integer N representing the number of predictions.
Line 2: N space-separated integers denoting confidence scores (0-100).
Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learni.outputFormat:
Line 1: 'High: X, Medium: Y, Low: Z' where X, Y, Z are counts.
Line 2: 'Average: W' where W is the average formatted to 1 decimal place.

Python with Data Science.title: Highest Grossing Customer Identifier
Python with Data Science.scenario: An online marketplace aggregates daily transaction receipts. Each transaction record lists a customer ID and the purchase amount. Calculate the cumulative spend per customer and identify the top customer. If multiple customers tie for the highest total spend, select the customer with the numerically smaller customer ID.
Python with Data Science.inputFormat:
Line 1: An integer N denoting the number of transaction records.
Next N lines: Two space-separated integers, customerId and amount.
Python with Data Science.explanation:
Customer 101: 250 + 300 = 550
Customer 102: 400 + 100 = 500
Customer 103: 550
Both 101 and 103 spent 550. Customer 101 is chosen because 101 < 103.

Python with Machine Learning.title: Automated Depot Dispatcher
Python with Machine Learning.scenario: A logistics facility operates autonomous shuttles along a straight 1D track. Charging stations are situated at integer coordinates X_1, X_2, ..., X_N. When a shuttle finishes a run at position T, it must dock at the nearest charging station (minimizing |X_i - T|). If two stations are equally distant, choose the station with the smaller coordinate.
Python with Machine Learning.inputFormat:
Line 1: Two space-separated integers N and T (dock count and shuttle position).
Line 2: N space-separated integers representing dock coordinates.
Python with Machine Learning.outputFormat: A single integer denoting the coordinate of the selected charging station.
Python with Machine Learning.explanation:
Distances to position 32:
|10 - 32| = 22
|25 - 32| = 7
|40 - 32| = 8
|55 - 32| = 23
|70 - 32| = 38
The closest dock is at 25 (distance 7).

Data Analytics.title: Regional Sales Runner-up
Data Analytics.scenario: A regional retail analytics dashboard determines annual bonus tiers. Management presents the silver award to the store with the second highest total revenue. If multiple stores tie for highest or any position, identical revenues share the same rank. Find the second highest distinct revenue figure. If all stores report identical revenues, output 'NO RUNNER UP'.
Data Analytics.inputFormat:
Line 1: An integer N representing the number of reporting stores.
Line 2: N space-separated integers representing store revenues.
Data Analytics.outputFormat: The second largest distinct revenue integer, or 'NO RUNNER UP'.
Data Analytics.explanation:
Distinct revenue values in descending order: 620, 580, 490, 450, 310.
The second largest distinct value is 580.

App Development.title: Push Notification Stream Compaction
App Development.scenario: A mobile push daemon receives a burst sequence of category tags. When rapid retries occur, identical consecutive tags flood user devices. To optimize packet delivery, compress consecutive runs of identical alert tags into the tag followed by its run count.
App Development.inputFormat:
Line 1: An integer N representing the number of notification tags in the stream.
Line 2: N space-separated strings representing the incoming tags.
App Development.outputFormat: Space-separated pairs formatted as '<TAG> <COUNT>' for each consecutive sequence.
App Development.constraints:
1 <= N <= 10^5
Each tag is alphanumeric (length 1 to 20)
App Development.sampleInput:
7
ALERT ALERT PUSH EMAIL EMAIL EMAIL PUSH
App Development.explanation:
Consecutive runs:
- ALERT: 2
- PUSH: 1
- EMAIL: 3
- PUSH: 1
Result: ALERT 2 PUSH 1 EMAIL 3 PUSH 1

Internet of Things (IOT).title: Greenhouse Temperature Spike Detector
Internet of Things (IOT).scenario: An agricultural IoT node takes hourly temperature readings in an automated greenhouse. A 'heat spike' is defined as any consecutive reading where the temperature rises by at least D degrees compared to the previous hour. Count the total number of heat spikes and find the single maximum surge (temperature increase) recorded.
Internet of Things (IOT).inputFormat:
Line 1: Two space-separated integers N and D (reading count and spike threshold).
Line 2: N space-separated integers representing consecutive hourly temperatures.
Internet of Things (IOT).outputFormat: Two space-separated integers: <total_spikes> <max_surge>. If no spikes occurred, print '0 0'.
Internet of Things (IOT).explanation:
Differences from previous hour:
22 -> 26: +4 (>= 3, spike!)
26 -> 25: -1
25 -> 30: +5 (>= 3, spike!)
30 -> 29: -1
29 -> 35: +6 (>= 3, spike!)
Total spikes = 3. Max surge = 6.

Embedded System.title: Sensor Frame Parity Verifier
Embedded System.scenario: An embedded controller receives serial 8-bit sensor frames. A frame is valid if the number of set bits (1s) in its binary representation is even (even parity). Count the number of valid frames received and compute their aggregate sum. If no frames are valid, output '0 0'.
Embedded System.inputFormat:
Line 1: An integer N representing the number of sensor frames.
Line 2: N space-separated integers (0 <= value <= 255).
Embedded System.explanation:
Binary set bits:
3 = 00000011 (2 bits, even -> VALID)
5 = 00000101 (2 bits, even -> VALID)
7 = 00000111 (3 bits, odd -> INVALID)
12 = 00001100 (2 bits, even -> VALID)
15 = 00001111 (4 bits, even -> VALID)
Valid frames: 3, 5, 12, 15 (count = 4). Sum = 3 + 5 + 12 + 15 = 35.
